newsitem.title: UK: WPP profits gain, promises further growth.
newsitem.headline: WPP profits gain, promises further growth.

text.p: WPP Group Plc , owner of advertising agencies Ogilvy & Mather and J Walter Thompson, Thursday posted a 15 percent profit gain in the first half of the year and forecast continuing strong growth.

Pre-tax profit for the first half of 1997 rose 15 percent to 78.3 million pounds ($124.2 million). WPP, which generates 80 percent of its earnings overseas, said the profit increase was over 25 percent at constant currency levels.
"The board does anticipate significant further progress even in its reported numbers and even if sterling's strength continues," the company said.

WPP forecast market growth in the 5-6 percent range in 1998, slightly lower than this year. Chief Executive Martin Sorrell said 1999 was expected to produce similar growth, but that 2000 may see an improvement.

"In the year 2000 we have the Millennium Olympics, we have the U.S. presidential election, we have the Millennium events as well, which will probably drive expenditure to better levels," he told Reuters Financial Television.
The first-half figures were at the top end of analysts' expectations.

The company, brought to its knees by the burden of debt in the early 1990s, said average net debt had fallen by 39 percent to 103 million pounds ($163 million). Debt has been whittled down from 372 million pounds ($590 million) four years ago.
Revenue was flat at 830.6 million pounds ($1.3 billion), as the rise in the value of the pound sterling wiped out what would have been an 8 percent rise at constant rates.
WPP said prospects for the second part of 1997 look similar to the first six months, adding that July revenues appeared to be up almost 7 percent if the effects of currencies were discounted.
